text: . In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold plunged nearly 4.4 per cent to 1,23,893 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver also tumbled over 4.9 per cent to 1,52,528 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. The combined Index of Core Industries (ICI) registered growth of 10.9 per cent in October on an annual basis driven by strong performance in iron ore, coal, electricity and cement sectors. This is higher than the upwardly revised growth rate of 8.2 per cent recorded in September. According to the provisional estimates released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry today, six out of nine core sectors recorded positive growth last month. Among these, iron ore production recorded the highest growth at 26.4 per cent. Coal production accelerated by 23.1 per cent, electricity generation increased by 21.6 per cent, cement production gained 15.4 per cent, steel production output grew by 7.3 per cent, and refinery products expanded by 3.4 per cent on an annual basis. However, natural gas production fell by 7.6 per cent, crude oil production dipped by 4.1 per cent, and fertilizer production declined by 12.2 per cent in October on an annual basis.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. India has called for stronger collaboration among BRICS member and partner countries in cinema, film co-productions, content distribution and the wider creative economy, with a focus on building sustained partnerships across the film industry.Addressing the BRICS Roundtable organised as part of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, A. S. Prabhat, said that cinema has a unique ability to bring people together by promoting cultural understanding, empathy and dialogue through shared human experiences. He highlighted that the BRICS Film Festival section at IFFI features 21 films from member and partner countries, covering themes such as democracy, indigenous identity, women’s rights, migration, climate change and social transformation. Mr. Prabhat also highlighted the BRICS Film Bazaar held in Mumbai on the 6th and 7th of August this year, which brought together filmmakers, producers, distributors and other creative industry professionals.Emphasising the need to expand cooperation beyond film showcases, he called for greater collaboration in animation, visual effects, gaming, emerging technologies and capacity building. He also expressed hope that the Roundtable would help translate the growing interest among participating countries into sustained institutional and industry-level partnerships.Joint Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs, Shambhu L. Hakki, said that the cinema serves as a powerful medium of cultural exchange, enabling societies to share their stories, perspectives and lived experiences, while fostering mutual understanding across borders. He noted that the screening of more than 20 films from BRICS member and partner countries would promote cultural exchange, friendship and mutual understanding. He emphasised the need to move beyond film showcases and encourage sustained collaboration among film institutions, production houses and creative industry professionals.Addressing the event, Chairman of the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), G. Krishnakumar, said that cinema is much more than an art form and serves as an important medium of cultural understanding. He highlighted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is working towards becoming a global hub of creativity. He added that the BRICS Film Bazaar brought together 1,126 delegates from across the expanded BRICS ecosystem, providing opportunities to explore cooperation in emerging technologies and the creative economy.Deputy Consul General of the Russian Federation in Mumbai, Aleksandr Fursov, has highlighted the growing cooperation among BRICS countries in cinema, including the establishment of the Association of BRICS Film Schools to promote student and faculty exchanges and collaborative film projects. Addressing the Roundtable, he said this year’s festival has integrated the BRICS Film Festival with WAVES Film Bazaar, providing new opportunities for collaboration. He noted that Russia, the partner country at IFFI this year, is presenting the archival musical comedy Cheryomushki and has set up a Russian pavilion at WAVES Film Bazaar, featuring 10 leading companies showcasing films, television series and animation.High Commissioner of the Federal Republic of Nigeria to India, Muhammad Saidu Dahiru, has described cinema as a powerful instrument of cultural diplomacy that promotes cultural identity, shared values and people-to-people connections. He highlighted the contribution of Nigeria’s vibrant film industry, including Nollywood and the regional Kannywood industry, to the country’s creative economy. He also welcomed the screening of the Nigerian film Lady at the IFFI 2026, saying that it would provide an opportunity to showcase Nigerian cinema and its creative talent to international audiences.CEO of the Entertainment Society of Goa, Dipak Bandekar, along with other dignitaries and representatives from BRICS member and partner countries, attended the roundtable.

. India’s Under-20 boys’ kabaddi team began their campaign at the Four-Nation Cup Kabaddi Championship 2026 in Kathmandu with a convincing 76-21 victory over Bangladesh, winning by a margin of 55 points.In another match, hosts Nepal defeated Thailand 56-50 to register a six-point victory. India currently tops the points table, while Nepal occupies the second position.The tournament features four teams- India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Thailand. Under the tournament format, each team will play the other teams once in a six-match league stage, with the top two teams qualifying for the final tomorrow.

. Ace Indian shuttler Lakshya Sen entered the men’s singles semifinals of the Hong Kong Open Badminton with a three-game win over former world champion Loh Kean Yew of Singapore in Kowloon today. Lakshya, who has already sealed his place in the BWF World Tour Finals, notched up an impressive 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 win over eighth seed Loh in the men’s singles quarterfinals. In another quarterfinal match, Kidambi Srikanth lost to Kunlavut Vitidsarn of Thailand 17-21, 7-21.Earlier, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty marched into the men’s doubles semifinals of the tournament with a three-game win 21-12, 13-21, 21-16 over China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yia. However, Rakshitha Ramraj’s dream run in women’s singles came to an end with a 19-21, 16-21 defeat to Thailand’s fifth seed Pornpawee Chochuwong in the quarterfinals.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has extended his greetings to National Cadet Corps (NCC) cadets and staff on NCC Day today. In a social media post Mr Singh said that the NCC embodies the spirit of unity, discipline and selfless service to the nation. He added that the NCC empowers the youth with leadership, character and a sense of national responsibility. The Defence Minister further said that the NCC reflects the strength of India’s diversity and the boundless potential of country’s youth.

. Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will be on a two-day visit to India from today. This will be his first visit to India after assuming office in March this year. On his arrival in New Delhi today, he will hold meeting with External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar. Tomorrow, the Nepal Prime Minister will call on President Droupadi Murmu and also meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi. During the bilateral talks, both Prime Ministers will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) in various areas will also be exchanged between the two countries.Akashvani Correspondent reports that the Ministry of External Affairs has said that the visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal under its ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. It added that the visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the bilateral partnership and advance mutually beneficial cooperation.The Ministry further said that India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors including trade and commerce, energy and water resources, and digital connectivity. The two countries also witnessed growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. Major Asian stock market indices edged lower today. Taiwan’s Taiex shed over 6.2 per cent, South Korea’s Kospi slumped 5.2 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell almost 5.1 per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times dipped nearly 2.1 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped 1.9 per cent, and China’s Shanghai Composite dipped 1.2 per cent.On the economic front, Japan’s consumer price index (CPI) rose to 2.3 per cent year-on-year in October, up from 2.1 per cent in September. Consumer prices exceeded the Bank of Japan’s two per cent target for the second straight month. Meanwhile, the core CPI, which strips out prices of food, rose to 2.2 per cent last month on an annual basis, higher than 2.1 per cent in the previous month.In European markets, Germany’s DAX dipped 1.8 per cent, and London’s FTSE 100 dropped half a per cent, when reports last came in.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis continue. Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh early today. It had also reported intercepting two ballistic missiles targeting Jazan on Friday. The coalition said it had targeted facilities at Hodeidah port, allegedly used for weapons and ballistic missile smuggling, and continued operations against Houthi military capabilities in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz. Yemen’s Houthi-run Saba news agency reported Saudi airstrikes in Taiz and Hajjah.IRGC-aligned Tasnim News Agency reported that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its Aerospace Force had detected, tracked and targeted a US MQ-9 drone using a new air defence system while monitoring aerial movements over the Strait of Hormuz. In a statement, the IRGC claimed the incident took the total number of US MQ-9 drones destroyed by Iran to 58, adding that surveillance over the strategic waterway was part of its efforts to safeguard the country’s security and sovereignty.

. Anupama Ramachandran clinched her second consecutive world title at the IBSF World Women’s Snooker Championship in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, yesterday. She defeated Hong Kong’s So Man Yan 3-1 in the final to successfully retain her crown, which she won last year to become India’s first-ever female IBSF Snooker world champion. After conceding a 16-58 defeat in the first frame, Anupama bounced back to win the next three frames dominantly to conquer the title in front of a home crowd.

. India’s capital markets have mobilised nearly 9 lakh crore rupees in the first seven months of the current financial year, while market capitalisation has crossed the 5 trillion-dollar mark. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has announced further regulatory reforms to attract foreign investment and simplify access to the country’s capital markets.Addressing the CII-DFS Financing Summit 2026 in Mumbai today, Mr Pandey said companies have raised an average of around 10 lakh crore rupees annually through equity and debt instruments over the past decade. He attributed the expansion to strong economic growth, rising investor participation and sustained regulatory reforms. More than 15 crore unique investors are now participating in the securities market.Highlighting the buoyancy in the primary market, the SEBI Chairman said 235 companies have raised around 1.5 lakh crore rupees through Initial Public Offerings so far in the current financial year.He said the corporate bond market is also emerging as an important source of business financing. Outstanding corporate bonds stood at around 62 lakh crore rupees in August this year, equivalent to nearly 55 per cent of bank credit extended to the industry and services sectors. Companies have raised more than 5 lakh crore rupees through bond issuances in FY 2026-27 so far.Mr Pandey also highlighted the growing contribution of Alternative Investment Funds in financing emerging businesses. Their cumulative investments reached around 7.5 lakh crore rupees by September, while committed capital exceeded 18 lakh crore rupees. Assets managed by Real Estate Investment Trusts and Infrastructure Investment Trusts have also crossed 10 lakh crore rupees, supporting infrastructure financing and capital recycling.On regulatory reforms, Mr Pandey said SEBI will soon release a consultation paper proposing further simplification of operations for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), including the removal of certain compliance requirements that are not prevalent in other major markets.He said the regulator is working to reduce the FPI onboarding period to as little as five business days. Around 740 FPIs have registered under the Swagat framework, accounting for 17 per cent of total FPI assets under custody.As part of the simplification measures, SEBI has digitised onboarding, permitted digitally signed powers of attorney and enabled net settlement to reduce funding costs. From 1st December, KYC review cycles for applicable FPIs will be extended from one and three years to two and eight years, respectively. Eligible NRIs, overseas citizens of India and foreign nationals can also complete their KYC and re-KYC digitally without travelling to India.Outlining future priorities, Mr Pandey said SEBI is reviewing ICDR and LODR frameworks to eliminate duplicate corporate filings and introduce a single-fine mechanism. It is also working with the RBI and Finance Ministry on a corporate bond market-making framework, reducing REIT and InvIT listing timelines to three working days, and expanding AI-based regulatory tools.On investor safety, he highlighted 45-minute disaster-recovery mandates, SEBI Check, validated UPI handles, and the nationwide ‘Samajh Se Investing Simple’ awareness campaign.

. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan have expressed grief over the demise of Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute. In a social media post, the President said that Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute was dedicated to the cause of public welfare and made valuable contributions to the development of Maharashtra and the nation.President Murmu extended her condolences to his family members, admirers and well-wishers.Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan has said Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute’s contributions to public life and service to the people will be remembered.

. In Hockey, India defeated South Korea 2-1 in their second league stage match of Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal yesterday evening. For India, Mumtaz Khan scored the first goal, while Sunelita Toppo scored India’s second goal. Hong Youngeun scored only goal for South Korea. Indian player Navneet Kaur was named Player of the Match. This was India’s second consecutive win in the tournament.Earlier in the day, Japan registered a convincing 3-nil victory over Thailand in their league stage encounter, while China and Malaysia played out a 2-2 draw. India will play its next match against Thailand today. The team will then face China on November 24 and Japan on November 25. The league stage will continue until November 25. Position matches will be played on November 27, followed by the bronze medal and gold medal matches on November 28.

. Netherlands Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen will arrive in New Delhi today on a two-day official visit to India, during which he is scheduled to hold discussions with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on strengthening bilateral cooperation across key sectors.Tomorrow, the Dutch Foreign Minister will hold a meeting with Mr. Vaishnaw. The visit comes as India and the Netherlands seek to expand their strategic partnership and strengthen cooperation across political, economic, commercial and technological domains. Mr Berendsen’s visit is expected to provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral cooperation and explore avenues for taking forward the India-Netherlands Strategic Partnership across priority sectors.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. Foreign Affairs Minister of Bulgaria Dr. Velislava Petrova-Chamova concluded her three day visit to India today. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar held delegation-level talks with Dr. Velislava Petrova-Chamova in New Delhi. External Affairs Ministry said that the two Ministers reviewed the entire gamut of bilateral relations. They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in trade and investment, infrastructure development, science and technology, AI, space, defence, education, culture, mobility and people-to-people exchanges.The Ministers expressed satisfaction at the deepening of ties between India and the EU. They also discussed regional and global issues, as well as cooperation in multilateral fora. The two sides have exchanged a joint roadmap to strengthen their partnership over the next five years.

. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor today hailed the India-U.S. partnership in cracking down on a transnational drug trafficking network under Operation Monsoon Thunder. In a social media post, Mr Gor said that India’s Narcotics Control Bureau, in close coordination with the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), disrupted the network allegedly supplying illegal drugs to consumers across the United States and apprehended six individuals. Mr Gor thanked Home Minister Amit Shah for his leadership and described the action as an example of the India-US partnership.The Narcotics Control Bureau of India has successfully busted the Indian module of a transnational drug trafficking network facilitating the supply of psychotropic and opioid drugs within the United States in close coordination with the US DEA under Operation Monsoon Thunder. NCB said that the network operated through digital platforms, including Telegram and WhatsApp, with Google Sheets used for managing orders. The law enforcement agency informed that six individuals have been apprehended during the operation; approximately three thousand parcels involving nearly 500 thousand tablets were identified, which were shipped within the USA; data relating to over 59 thousand US subjects was shared with the US DEA; and two live consignments were intercepted by the US DEA.The agency said that the operation underscored the strength of India-US law enforcement cooperation and the commitment of both agencies to dismantling transnational drug trafficking networks. It further added that NCB India remains committed to combating drug trafficking through intelligence-led enforcement and strong international partnerships.

. World Fisheries Day is being observed today. The day aims to highlight the importance of sustainable fisheries and aquaculture in ensuring food and nutritional security, generating livelihoods and maintaining ecological balance. The observance traces its origins to 1997, when representatives from 18 countries gathered in New Delhi to establish the World Fisheries Forum. The initiative aimed to promote responsible fishing practices and safeguard the rights and interests of fishing communities.The theme for World Fisheries Day 2026 is “Empowering People for Change: Advancing Decent Work in Fisheries and Aquaculture, Particularly for Youth and Women.” The theme highlights the need to promote decent employment opportunities, empower women and young people, and ensure inclusive and sustainable growth across the fisheries and aquaculture sectors.India is the world’s second-largest fish-producing country, accounting for nearly eight per cent of global fish production. The country has made significant progress in the sector over the past decade. India’s total fish production has more than doubled, rising from 96 lakh tonnes to 195 lakh tonnes last year. The fisheries sector is an important pillar of the Indian economy, supporting the livelihoods of millions of people. A coordinated approach involving all stakeholders is aimed at further strengthening the sector, with a focus on increasing fish production, boosting exports and creating more livelihood opportunities.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed happiness over people buying less gold following an appeal made by him last year. Addressing a function in Lucknow, Mr Modi said, people cut back on buying gold after his appeal, which helped bring gold prices down and allowed buyers to save money. Prime Minister had appealed to the nation to avoid buying gold, when India’s foreign exchange came under pressure with the West Asia conflict pushing up crude prices. Mr Modi drew a parallel between the public’s response to his appeal and how Indians historically heeded former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri’s call to skip one meal, stating that the country still holds that same character.Gold prices have seen a major decline over the past few months. 24-carat gold prices fell to 12,523 rupees per gram yesterday from 15,250 per gram on May 9, this year. Gold imports fell nearly 40% during April-October 2026.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. In the forex market today, the rupee strengthened by 62 paise to close at a seven-month high of 92 rupees and 67 paise against the US dollar. The rupee extended its rising streak for the fifth consecutive session following uninterrupted inflow of foreign funds and a rally in domestic stock markets.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.85 in intra-day trade.

. The makers of the Russian feature film New Home interacted with the media at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today.Director Nikita Grushin and Director of Photography Ekaterina Smolina addressed a press conference at the IFFI Media Centre in Panaji. The film is being showcased in the International Cinema section as part of the Russian Federation’s Partner Country presentation.The film follows Anna, a woman released from prison after seven years, as she struggles to rebuild her life. With support from social services and a support group, where she meets Roman, she begins a journey towards healing and a fresh start.Speaking about the inspiration behind the film, Director Nikita Grushin highlighted how feelings of guilt, often hidden in the subconscious mind, can influence human behaviour. He stressed the importance of understanding these emotions and turning negative experiences into positive actions.Cinematographer Ekaterina Smolina shared her journey of entering the field of cinematography at the age of 30. She spoke about overcoming fear and following her passion for photography. She also encouraged women to pursue their creative ambitions without hesitation.

. The 3rd All India Police Badminton Cluster 2026-27 is currently underway at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Naranpura, Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Hosted by the Gujarat Police, the national-level championship has entered an exciting phase following impressive performances on the second day of the tournament.Today, a total of 328 matches are scheduled to be played across different categories, including 90 matches in badminton and 238 in table tennis. During yesterday’s second-day events, police athletes from various states and Central Armed Police Forces delivered strong performances across knockout and individual rounds. Hosts Gujarat have also put up an impressive show, particularly in the women’s badminton category.The six-day tournament, which concludes on November 24, features over 1,150 police personnel representing 38 teams from 24 states, four Union Territories, and ten Central Armed Police Forces, including the CRPF, BSF, and CISF. Promoting camaraderie and fitness without rank barriers, the event brings together 463 gazetted officers and 699 non-gazetted personnel, including Gujarat DGP Gyanendra Singh Malik.

. US President Donald Trump has said that any potential agreement with Iran must be permanent and aimed at preventing Tehran from acquiring nuclear weapons. In an interview with a private news channel, Trump said he is not particularly interested in regime change in Iran, but described the attacks on the country’s senior leadership as a significant shift. He called Iran’s new leadership more rational but questioned its reliability in negotiations, alleging that Tehran has repeatedly broken previous agreements.His remarks come amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with Trump insisting that any deal must meet US expectations. Earlier, following his visit to China, Trump accused Iran of misleading the international community for decades.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the ninth Pre-Budget Consultation with  experts and stakeholders from the housing, urbanisation, and culture sectors in connection with the Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was also attended by Secretaries of Department of Economic Affairs and Department of Urban Development.Earlier in the day, the Finance Minister chaired the eighth Pre-Budget Consultation with the stakeholders from employment and labour sectors in connection with the upcoming Union Budget. The meeting was attended by Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur and senior officials from Ministry of Labour and Employment.The Finance Ministry conducts several pre-Budget consultation meetings annually with experts, industry leaders, economists, and state officials. The deliberations seek to ensure the Union budget reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key economic priorities.

. Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

. The United States has rejected Iranian claims that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) damaged a US F-16 fighter aircraft, saying that all its military fighter jets in the Middle East are safe and accounted for.In a social media post, the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said Iran had not attacked a US F-16. Iranian state media had earlier reported that the aircraft was targeted by the IRGC and forced to make an emergency landing.Meanwhile, the IRGC has claimed that it carried out a combined missile and drone operation targeting two US Patriot air defence radars at military bases in Bahrain. Its Aerospace Force said it struck US military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases. The IRGC described the operation as retaliation for alleged repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US MQ-1 and MQ-9 drones, as well as an attack on a radar installation on Iran’s Hengam Island. It warned that Iranian airspace was a “red line” and that further violations would invite a “harsh and decisive response”.Bahrain, however, has rejected the claim of damage to the US radar systems while reporting multiple Iranian attacks. Its Ministry of Interior said a civilian industrial facility was targeted, triggering a fire and causing material damage, but no injuries were reported. The Bahrain Defence Forces also said their air defence systems intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks yesterday. Debris from the interceptions fell in some residential areas, causing minor material damage, with no injuries.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia said its air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile in the western region and a drone launched towards the Riyadh area. In the early hours of Sunday, the country’s National Early Warning Platform issued an alert for Makkah Province, warning residents of potential danger.The Houthis, however, denied posing any threat to Makkah. Houthi-aligned Al Masirah TV quoted the group’s military spokesperson as saying that its targets were limited to Saudi oil facilities and military installations, while describing Islamic holy sites as deserving the highest regard.With military activity continuing across multiple fronts, tensions in the region remain high.

. Nitesh Tiwari-directed Hindi film Ramayana: Rise of a Legend – Part 1 was screened at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today, marking the inauguration of the Films from BRICS section. The screening witnessed a full house, with film enthusiasts gathering in large numbers and displaying great excitement.Director Nitesh Tiwari, 57th IFFI Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.As part of the ceremony, the Heads of Missions (HoMs) of BRICS countries were felicitated by Shri G. Krishnakumar, Chairman, NFDC, and Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.Addressing the audience, Nitesh Tiwari thanked them for the love the film has been receiving. He also shared the inspiration behind bringing the epic Ramayana to the big screen on a grand scale and expressed his honour at being part of the 57th IFFI.The film opened the BRICS Special Section, featuring 21 films from all 11 BRICS member countries and partner nations, celebrating diverse stories and cultures while fostering cultural exchange through cinema.

. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) yesterday proposed eliminating additional disclosure requirements for offshore funds, arguing that existing beneficial ownership disclosure norms already provide adequate transparency and oversight. The proposal marks a significant shift from regulations introduced in 2023, when the market regulator tightened scrutiny of offshore investment structures. Under the current framework, offshore funds considered to be at higher risk are required to make enhanced disclosures, including details of their ultimate beneficial owners.The regulator said the proposed changes are aimed at balancing regulatory oversight with ease of doing business while ensuring that capital markets remain attractive to foreign investors. The proposal has been put forward for public consultation, and feedback from market participants is expected before SEBI takes a final decision on amending the framework.

. In Badminton, India’s Lakshya Sen’s 13-match winning streak came to an end after he suffered a straight-games defeat to Denmark’s World No. 3 Anders Antonsen in the men’s singles semifinal of the Hong Kong Open today. World No. 11 Sen went down 13-21, 13-21 against the Danish shuttler. Sen had stormed into the semifinals after defeating Singapore’s former world champion and eighth seed Loh Kean Yew 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 in the quarterfinals. With this defeat, India’s campaign at the Hong Kong Open came to an end.Earlier, India’s men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty crashed out of the tournament after losing their semifinal clash against Malaysia’s Tee Kai Wun and Man Wei Chong. The Indian duo went down 18-21, 19-21 in straight games, bringing their campaign at the Hong Kong Open to an end.

. India today scored 486 for 4 at stumps on Day 3 of the opening Test against hosts New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. The Visitors finished the day with a significant 118-run first-innings lead over the hosts, who were dismissed for 368.KL Rahul slammed a historic century, producing a magnificent 136 off 290 deliveries, with the help of nine fours and two sixes. Rahul also became the first Indian opening batter to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries, South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.  Rahul received excellent support from Devdutt Padikkal, who scored a valuable 80 runs. The duo stitched together a brilliant century partnership to strengthen India’s position.Earlier, India won the toss and elected to bowl. The Indian pace attack, led by Jasprit Bumrah, reduced New Zealand to 70 for five. However, a remarkable sixth-wicket partnership helped the hosts stage a recovery. Henry Nicholls remained unbeaten on 140 off 282 deliveries, while Glenn Phillips scored 118 off 216 balls to guide New Zealand to a strong total. The two-match Test series is the final leg of India’s tour of New Zealand, with crucial ICC World Test Championship points at stake.

. Rajya Sabha Member of Parliament Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute passed away today at the age of 72 while undergoing treatment at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi. He was admitted to the hospital following a heart attack. Despite medical treatment, he could not be revived.Ramrao Wadkute was a prominent political figure from the Marathwada region and was widely recognised for his work on issues concerning the Dhangar community.He began his political journey through the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and served as a Member of the Maharashtra Legislative Council from 2004 to 2019. During his political career, he held several important responsibilities, including Chairman of the Maharashtra State Cooperative Milk Federation and Chairman of the Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Sheep and Goat Development Corporation.The BJP nominated Ramrao Wadkute for the Rajya Sabha from Maharashtra in March 2026. His parliamentary term began in April, and he took the oath as a Rajya Sabha member during the same month.

. The 57th International Film Festival of India is bringing back some of India’s timeless cinematic treasures through its Restored Classics showcase, giving audiences an opportunity to rediscover the magic of films that have shaped the country’s cinematic history. Presented by the National Film Development Corporation – National Film Archive of India, the films have been restored under the National Film Heritage Mission of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Classics like Kashmir Ki Kali, Waqt, Kabhi Kabhi, Thulabharam are being screened after being restored.The vision behind this initiative is not merely to preserve old films, but to safeguard India’s rich cinematic heritage, revive its artistic brilliance and make these masterpieces accessible to younger generations.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended over one per cent higher for the second straight session today. The Sensex jumped 898 points to close at 83,920. The Nifty climbed 286 points to settle at 25,801.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained almost 0.7 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index dipped over 0.1 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 20 out of 30 constituent companies logged gains. Among the top performers, Kotak Mahindra Bank as well as HDFC Bank jumped over three per cent, Maruti surged nearly 2.9 per cent, and UltraTech Cement climbed almost 2.8 per cent. In contrast, Titan as well as Tata Steel fell 1.7 per cent, NTPC dropped 1.3 per cent, and Hindustan Unilever shed almost one per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 22 out of 28 sectors edged higher. Among the top gainers, Hospitals jumped 3.6 per cent, Private Banks advanced nearly 2.7 per cent and Top 10 Banks added almost two and a half per cent. In contrast, Telecommunication as well as Consumer Durables dropped 0.6 per cent, Industrials lost half a per cent, and Capital Goods dipped nearly half per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,575 companies declined, 1,804 advanced and 243 remained unchanged.

. Ace Indian shuttler Lakshya Sen will take on Denmark’s Anders Antonsen in the men’s singles semifinal of the Hong Kong Open Badminton Tournament today. Sen stormed into the semifinals after defeating former world champion and eighth seed Loh Kean Yew of Singapore 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 in the quarterfinals in Kowloon.Meanwhile, the Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will face Malaysia’s Tee Kai Wun and Man Wei Chong in their semifinal clash. The Indian duo entered the last four after registering an impressive 21-12, 13-21, 21-16 victory over China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi in the quarterfinals.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed grief over the loss of lives in a mishap at, Kutch Gujarat. Mr. Modi conveyed his condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured. The Prime Minister has also announced an ex-gratia of two lakh rupees from Prime Minister National Relief Fund (PMNRF) to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. He further announced that the injured would be given fifty thousand rupees from the PMNRF.

. In Men’s Cricket, New Zealand scored 119 for 2 at stumps on Day Four of the first Test against India in their second innings at Wellington.Earlier, the Visitors declared their first innings at a record 720 for 9, taking a huge lead of 352 runs over New Zealand’s first-innings score of 368. India’s total of 720 is their highest-ever Test score outside India and the 18th-highest total in Test cricket history.India also created two major records and became the first team to have their top five batters score 80 or more runs in the same innings. They also became the first team to build partnerships of 50 or more runs for each of the first seven wickets.For Visitors, KL Rahul played a key role at the top of the order. He became the first Indian opener to score a Test century in all four SENA countries South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

. Union Minister of Food Processing Industries Chirag Paswan has urged beverage companies to innovate and offer healthier beverage alternatives using indigenous superfoods like makhana, millets and sattu. Addressing the Indian Beverage Association Conclave 2026 in New Delhi, the Minister called upon leaders in the food processing industry to build globally recognised Indian Quick Service Restaurant brands and achieve self-reliance in bottling and packaging machinery.Stressing on zero compromise with quality, Mr Paswan asked them to strengthen backward linkages with farmers and Farmer Producer Organisations to ensure uniform taste, meet global standards, and minimise post harvest wastage. The Minister further said that the Government is awared about the challenges faced by the beverage sector and aims to address them.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi flagged off the 99th edition of ‘Sunday on Cycle’ from Dandi Kutir in Gandhinagar today. Organized across 26,000 locations nationwide, the event commemorates Constitution Day through fitness.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya described cycling as a complete exercise and a key solution to traffic and pollution. He urged the youth to make cycling both a fashion and a passion, becoming fitness-conscious and nation-conscious to help realize the vision of ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047.He also announced that the milestone 100th edition will be held on November 29.Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi lauded Dr. Mandaviya’s consistency in driving the ‘Fit India’ and ‘Drugs-Free India’ initiatives, inspiring young citizens across the country. Both leaders later joined local cyclists and athletes in a bicycle rally to promote health awareness.

. President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have expressed grief over the loss of lives in the road accident in Kota, Rajasthan.In their social media posts, the President and the Vice President extended condolences to the families of the deceased and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.The Prime Minister also expressed grief over the mishap and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured. He also announced an ex-gratia of two lakh rupees from Prime Minister National Relief Fund (PMNRF) to the next of kin of each of those who lost their lives. He further announced that the injured would be given fifty thousand rupees from the PMNRF.

. A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country’s Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The ship – the Sparta II – caught on fire after the strike yesterday, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment. Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was no threat to the territory’s supplies.The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments. The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia’s defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.This prompted temporary aviation and maritime restrictions around the area, Finnish border officials said. A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad’s governor wrote on Telegram, adding that the crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way. The Finnish Border Guard later said the crew had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was now already en route to Russia. The Russian rescue vessel had remained at the location of the stricken ship.

. The United Nations has expressed deep concern over the escalating hostilities in and around Yemen. Deputy Spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General, Farhan Haq, urged all parties to uphold their obligations under international humanitarian law, particularly the prohibition against targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure.Farhan Haq called on all parties to take constant care to protect the civilian population and civilian objects from the effects of hostilities. UN humanitarian agencies also warned that civilians in Yemen continue to bear the brunt of escalating violence, compounded by severe restrictions on humanitarian access.Meanwhile, in Yemen, at least 41 people were killed in airstrikes attributed to Saudi Arabia over the past 24 hours. Citing health authorities in the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, Houthi-run Media reported that 28 people were injured in the attacks. Houthi military spokesperson said in a statement that the group targeted the Al-Shuqaiq power plant and Jazan port in Saudi Arabia’s Jazan region. On the other hand, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles targeting Jazan. It had also reported intercepting three ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh early today.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 0.6 per cent down at 91 US dollars and 44 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.2 per cent down at 82 US dollars and 27 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will be on a two-day visit to India starting tomorrow. This will be his first visit to India after assuming office in March this year. On his arrival in New Delhi tomorrow, he will hold a meeting with External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar. The next day, the Nepal Prime Minister will call on President Droupadi Murmu and also meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi. During the bilateral talks, both the Prime Ministers will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) in various areas will also be exchanged between the two countries.The Ministry of External Affairs said that India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors including trade and commerce, energy and water resources, and digital connectivity.The two countries also witnessed growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports. The visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal under its ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. It will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the bilateral partnership and advance mutually beneficial cooperation.

. In Hockey, India defeated South Korea 2-1 in their second league stage match of Women’s Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal this evening. For India, Mumtaz Khan scored the first goal in the 30th minute, while Sunelita Toppo Sunelita scored India’s second goal. Hong Youngeun scored only goal for South Korea. Earlier in the day, Japan registered a convincing 3-nil victory over Thailand in their league stage encounter, while China and Malaysia played out a 2-2 draw.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed grief over the passing of Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute. In a social media post, Mr. Modi said that Ramrao Wadkute will be remembered for his contribution to society and emphasis on serving the poor and downtrodden. He further said that Ramrao’s efforts were dedicated to strengthen the BJP in Maharashtra. The Prime Minister extended his condolences to Ramrao’s family members and admirers.
